climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Loess is fine, wind-blown silt. Fertile and warm, it holds water well but drains poorly.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
